prompt: Write 10 distinct short extracts of Larkmere Mutual's official guidance, procedures or policy wording about: an attorney managing a parent's account. Two to four sentences each, in the society's own formal voice. Use type "fact". Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"fact","content":"If you have authority to act as an attorney for a member, you may manage the account only within the scope of the power granted. We will need sight of the original or a certified copy of the lasting power of attorney, or equivalent legal authority, before we can register the arrangement. Until registration is complete, we may be unable to accept instructions from you."},{"type":"fact","content":"An attorney must satisfy our identification and verification checks before access is granted. We may ask for evidence of your name, address and authority to act, and we may carry out additional checks where required by law. These checks are designed to protect the member and the account."},{"type":"fact","content":"Where there is more than one attorney, we will follow the instructions set out in the legal document. If the document states that attorneys must act jointly, we will require all appointed attorneys to sign or agree as instructed. If it permits them to act independently, we may accept instructions from any one attorney acting alone."},{"type":"fact","content":"An attorney may use the account to manage the member’s everyday banking, pay bills and make routine enquiries, subject to the powers granted. You must always act in the member’s best interests and not use the account for your own benefit unless the authority expressly permits this. We may refuse any instruction that appears inconsistent with the legal authority provided."},{"type":"fact","content":"If a parent has mental capacity and wishes to continue dealing with the account, we will normally act on the member’s own instructions. The attorney’s authority does not usually override the member’s right to act for themselves while they remain able to do so. Where there is doubt, we may ask for further evidence or seek clarification of the legal position."},{"type":"fact","content":"We may place restrictions on certain account features when an attorney is registered. This may include limits on new borrowing, changes to nominated payees, or requests to close products, depending on the terms of the authority and the account type. Any restriction we apply will be consistent with our legal and regulatory obligations."},{"type":"fact","content":"An attorney must tell us promptly if the member dies, loses capacity, recovers capacity, or the power of attorney is revoked. We may suspend the attorney’s access while we review the position. This helps us ensure that only valid instructions are acted upon."},{"type":"fact","content":"We will send account communications to the correspondence address we hold, which may be the attorney’s address if requested and appropriate. We may ask for supporting records if we need to verify how funds have been used."},{"type":"fact","content":"If we receive conflicting instructions from the member and the attorney, we will decide how to proceed according to the authority in place and applicable law.
